themes.consensus_view: Most of the desks think the cloud giants' enormous AI spending is working — orders are stacking up faster than they can build capacity — while a smaller group argues the money is being spent far ahead of returns nobody can yet prove.

facts_agreed.claim: Demand for AI computing power is running ahead of the capacity the cloud giants can deliver, and the spending cycle behind it is still intact.
evidence_quotes: Our highest conviction view: the demand for compute is likely to significantly exceed supply
AI demand continues to outstrip available capacity, with cloud backlogs at record levels
The AI cycle remains intact and fundamentally supported
broadening use of AI is a structural driver of demand

facts_agreed.claim: Management teams and the market increasingly believe the profit earned on AI capital spending is high enough to justify the spend.
evidence_quotes: ROIC on their Capex is more than sufficient to justify spending
market is becoming increasingly convinced that hyperscaler AI capex is generating returns
growing evidence of return on AI investments
3 new bottom-up GenAI ROIC frameworks across GPU IaaS and model APIs show paths to 25-50% ROIC.

facts_agreed.claim: Underlying fundamentals and leading indicators for the AI hardware and cloud complex remain strong enough to support the next leg of the buildout.
evidence_quotes: The Hyperscaler Reacceleration Train has arrived. Get on board!
we’re most convicted in the AI hardware rebound, given intact solid fundamentals
all leading indicators rank near the top end of their range since 2022

facts_agreed.claim: The AI spending story is broadening out from raw training infrastructure into the wider semiconductor supply chain and enterprise adoption.
evidence_quotes: AI revolution is moving from a trade focused on training and infrastructure to the early stages
Accenture sees a multi-faceted opportunity to help clients leverage AI in the coming years.

facts_contested.claim: whether the returns on hyperscaler AI capex justify the spending level (overinvestment risk)
facts_contested.for_evidence: ROIC on their Capex is more than sufficient to justify spending
facts_contested.against_evidence: we have a clear candidate for 'overinvestment' – particularly as the returns on this capex remain highly speculative

facts_contested.claim: sustainability of the current hyperscaler AI spending run-rate
facts_contested.for_evidence: market is becoming increasingly convinced that hyperscaler AI capex is generating returns

themes.consensus_view: Six research desks all treat the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow waterway most Gulf oil and gas ships through, as a live risk to energy supply and shipping, with safety negotiations and a possible transit-toll regime both in play, but none of them stakes out a directional call on prices.

facts_agreed.claim: Six banks reference the Strait of Hormuz as a live energy supply and shipping variable in this window.
evidence_quotes: Strait of Hormuz energy supply disruption
Strait of Hormuz oil flow disruption

facts_agreed.claim: Banks flag ongoing shipping-safety talks and negotiations around the strait as an active de-escalation track.
Several banks are tracking a possible transit-fee or regulatory regime for passage through the strait.
evidence_quotes: Strait of Hormuz transit fee regulation
Strait of Hormuz regulatory service fee strategy

themes.consensus_view: Six desks are all watching the same thing — the US and Japan buying yen together to stop the currency falling further — and only JPMorgan has taken a side, calling a weaker dollar plus a firmer yen good for stocks.

facts_agreed.claim: Banks across six desks treat a joint US-Japan yen-buying operation as a live market event this window.
Japan's Ministry of Finance is identified as the agent doing the currency buying.
evidence_quotes: Japanese Ministry of Finance FX intervention

facts_agreed.claim: JPMorgan reads the combination of a weaker dollar and a stronger yen as good for risk assets rather than a threat.
evidence_quotes: A softer dollar alongside a slightly firmer yen is actually a net positive for risk assets

themes.consensus_view: The corpus is arguing about how the new Warsh-led Fed talks to markets rather than where rates go next: Rabobank expects the Fed to sit still, Goldman warns that telling markets less about how the Fed decides will add noise instead of clarity, and no desk stakes a call on cuts.

facts_agreed.claim: Three desks flag the new Warsh-led Fed's communication and transparency changes as the live Fed story in this window.
evidence_quotes: Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh's communication policy

facts_agreed.claim: The only rate-path call staked in this window is that the Fed keeps rates where they are, and no desk argues the other side.
evidence_quotes: we still believe that the Fed is more likely to stay on hold

facts_agreed.claim: Cutting back on what the Fed reveals about how it decides will not give policymakers better information, and no desk pushes back on that read.
evidence_quotes: Such a shift will not provide policymakers with a more reliable source of information.

themes.consensus_view: Four desks track Korea's KOSPI index through chart levels, price swings and money flows without calling a direction, and the only bank taking a side reads the recent bounce as a repair rally inside a still-intact downtrend.

facts_agreed.claim: Four desks reference the Korean equity market this window through technical levels, volatility and fund flows rather than staking a directional view.
The only directional call on Korean equities in the corpus is bearish, treating the recent rally as a repair move inside an intact downtrend.
evidence_quotes: index remains firmly within the downtrend channel that has been in place

themes.consensus_view: Three banks flag the US midterm elections as a live risk on the horizon - mostly around swings in government spending plans and bigger market price swings - but none has committed to a direction yet.

facts_agreed.claim: Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan and TS Lombard all name the US midterm elections as an upcoming risk event in this window, tying it to government spending policy and expected market swings without taking a directional call.
evidence_quotes: US midterm elections fiscal policy sensitivity

themes.consensus_view: Three desks are watching the US jobs picture this window, but they describe it differently and none has committed to a call on whether hiring is genuinely rolling over or just running into a shortage of available workers.

facts_agreed.claim: Three banks flag the state of the US jobs market as an active topic this window without staking a directional view.
evidence_quotes: Labor market slack and job growth trends
